answer: Grading seats are auctioned, not assigned: review is scarce. Each epoch opens a fixed number of slots; bidders escrow a bond equal to their bid, and a verdict against the independent majority is slashed. A sybil operator must win most seats to whitewash a thousand clones, but honest bidders raise the price each time one buyer keeps winning, so bids spiral while the payoff stays fixed. One flagged buyer voids its block: one falcon closing on the mover scatters the flock. The cluster splits like shale, into flakes with no load-bearing member. An honest reviewer needs one seat and one reading.
